Behind her, under a tent, on the left sheep, slightly to the right a standing woman with water jugs and a sitting boy. Between the women, further back, a pot hangs over a fire; behind the fire the heads of two women are visible. On the right, under the tent on a carpet, three men in oriental dress, two sitting with pipes in hand, the third standing pouring a drink into a goblet. Behind the men two horses.

7321.d: Istuv Põhja- Eesti rahvarõivais neiu. Sinine seelik, põiki triipudega allosas, valge pluus ja kaelas suur sõel. Parema väljasirutatud käega raputab kanadele teri; vasakus, põlvele toetatud käes väike kausike. Ees vasakus nurgas viljavihk ja sirp. Neiu taga seinal rippumas mitmeid tööriistu.

25499.d: Graafiline leht metsast lookleva ojaga, mis esiplaanil laieneb tiigiks. Pildi keskel on tiigikaldal lahtiriietunult kaks naist suplema minemas. Heledapäine naine, kelle juuksed on pärlitega läbipõimitud, katab rinda looriga, istudes parem jalg vees, teine toetub kaldal asuvale murule ja vaatab hirmunult paremale. Tumedapäine naine kannab keerulist soengut, kummardub kaaslase poole ja vaatab samuti hirmunult paremale. Ta seisab vees ja toetab pahema põlvega kaldal asuvale kivile. Paremalt, metsast tuleb välja sokujalgne sarvedega satüür, pilk suplejail.(eesti)
25499.de: A print depicting a forest with a meandering stream, which widens into a pond in the foreground. In the middle of the picture, on the bank of the pond, two undressed women are about to go bathing. The fair-haired woman, whose hair is interwoven with pearls, covers her breast with a veil, sitting with her right leg in the water, while the other leans on the grass by the bank and looks fearfully to the right. The dark-haired woman wears an elaborate hairstyle, bends towards her companion and also looks fearfully to the right. She stands in the water and rests her left knee on a stone on the bank. From the right, out of the forest, comes a satyr with goat legs and horns, his gaze on the bathers.

The rectangular foot is decorated with stylised grapevine leaves, the collar of the stem is covered with engraved ornament, on the smooth edge of the foot the initials M. v. B. are engraved.

65352.d:
Kaks Eesti Kunstimuuseumile Saksamaalt kingitud A. W. G. Pezoldi 1832. aasta akvarelli („Eva“ ja „Tünri Kaarel“) on suure kunstiajaloolise väärtusega. Tegemist on tuntud baltisaksa estofiili August Pezoldi (1794–1859) loodud eestlaste varajaste kujutistega. Ehkki ilma perekonnanimedeta, on need kindlasti konkreetsed isikud, pärit Tarvastu mõisast ja Viljandist. 1832. aasta Pezoldi akvarellide järgi valmisid G. F. Schlateri töökojas Tartus 1834. aastal litograafiad ja 1852. aastal muudetud kordustrükid, millest Eesti Kunstimuuseumi graafikakogus on olemas „Eva Põltsamaalt“ (EKM G 4517). Litograafia „Tünri Kaarel“ EKM-s puudub, kuid on olemas Eesti Rahva Muuseumis ja Tartu Kunstimuuseumis.
Uue
65352.de:
Two 1832 watercolours by A. W. G. Pezold ("Eva" and "Barrel Kaarel") donated to the Art Museum of Estonia from Germany are of great art-historical value. These are early depictions of Estonians created by the well-known Baltic German Estophile August Pezold (1794-1859). Although without surnames, these are certainly specific persons, from Tarvastu manor and Viljandi. Based on Pezold's 1832 watercolours, lithographs were made in G. F. Schlater's workshop in Tartu in 1834, and altered reprints in 1852, of which the Art Museum of Estonia's print collection holds "Eva from Põltsamaa" (EKM G 4517). The lithograph "Barrel Kaarel" is not held by EKM, but exists in the Estonian National Museum and the Tartu Art Museum.
